Hostel warden's note, third-year block, October. Over the term I have watched Pooja step back from the corridor group that ranks everyone by phones and outings. In August she was at every one of their dinners. By October she sat with them only on Fridays. She began studying in the common room with Salma, who cares nothing for the group's ranking, and the two share a kettle and long evening walks. Pooja looked lonely in September, eating alone twice. Once I saw her stand at the group's door with a hand raised, then walk away. Rhea, who leads the group, sent a message: “We miss you.”

What I did next: I did not comment on the group. I asked Pooja whether the common room key for evenings would help. She said yes.

qa.q: With whom did Pooja begin studying in the common room?
qa.a: Pooja began studying in the common room with Salma.

qa.q: What might Pooja have been feeling when standing at the group's door with a hand raised and then walking away?
qa.a: Pooja was probably lonely and torn, missing the old belonging but sure enough about the change to walk away.

qa.q: What did the warden choose to do rather than comment on the group?
qa.a: The warden asked Pooja whether the common room key for evenings would help, and did not comment on the group.

qa.q: What might Rhea be feeling as Pooja sits with the group only on Fridays?
qa.a: Rhea may feel puzzled and a little hurt, or worried about the group's standing, which may explain the message saying “We miss you.”

grounding: A hostel warden's note shows a young adult gradually leaving a status-focused group and investing in someone who does not rank them.

Saturday night. I did it again: skipped the rooftop thing with Meera's crowd. Nobody texted. That's the part that stings. Three months ago I checked my phone every ten minutes for their plans. Tonight I checked it just to see if anything was there, and it was empty. I ate dinner alone in the mess and hated it.

Then Uday messaged: “Dal-chawal at mine, come? No dress code, no ranking, lol.” I went. We watched an old film and argued about the ending, and I laughed until my ribs hurt. Nobody asked where my jacket was from.

I still miss the group a bit. But I slept better tonight than I have in weeks.
— Dilnaz

qa.q: What did Uday offer in the message?
qa.a: Uday offered dal-chawal at home with no dress code and no ranking.

qa.q: Why does the silence after skipping the rooftop event sting Dilnaz?
qa.a: Dilnaz used to check the phone for the group's plans, so the empty screen shows how much belonging was tied to that group.

qa.q: What choice did Dilnaz make after eating dinner alone?
qa.a: Dilnaz accepted Uday's invitation instead of staying alone or going back to the old crowd.

qa.q: What might Uday have been thinking when sending the message?
qa.a: Uday probably noticed Dilnaz slipping away and wanted to offer easy company with no pressure or ranking.

grounding: A young adult moves away from a status-focused group, feels lonely first and finds steadier belonging with someone who does not rank them.
